'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Afar–Somali clashes]]
**According to the government of [[Ethiopia]]'s [[Somali Region]], [[militant]]s from the [[Afar Region]] attack for the fourth day the [[Somali Region|Somali]] town of [[Garbaiisa]], killing up to 300 people. In response, protesters set up roadblocks along a highway leading to [[Djibouti]] and damaged parts of the [[Addis Ababa–Djibouti Railway]], threatening [[Economy of Ethiopia|Ethiopia's economy]]. This comes after multiple days of fighting between [[Afar people|Afar]] and [[Somalis|Somali]] militants in Garbaiisa. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/hundreds-civilians-killed-attack-ethiopias-somali-region-local-government-says-2021-07-27/ (Reuters)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-27/protests-block-djibouti-ethiopia-railway-somali-guardian-says (Bloomberg)]
*The [[Cuba]]n embassy in [[Paris]], [[France]], is attacked with three [[Molotov cocktail|molotovs]], resulting in a fire outside the building but without causing any injuries. The identities of the perpetrators of the attack are unknown. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/7/27/cuba-says-paris-embassy-targeted-with-petrol-bombs (Al Jazeera)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*The [[United States District Court for the Eastern District of New York|U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York]] orders American [[handicraft]] chain [[Hobby Lobby]] to forfeit a 3,600-year-old tablet containing a portion of the ''[[Epic of Gilgamesh]]'' to the federal government, after the company illegally purchased it in a private auction in 2014. The [[United States Department of Justice|Justice Department]] had been looking to claim the tablet since 2013, as it was suspected to have been stolen from an [[Iraq]]i archeological site in the aftermath of the [[Gulf War|1991 Gulf War]], so it could be repatriated back to Iraq. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/07/27/politics/epic-of-gilgamesh-hobby-lobby/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/politics-news/justice-department-seizes-rare-ancient-tablet-illegally-auctioned-hobby-lobby-n1275217 (NBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Leverkusen explosion]]
**Two people are killed, 31 are injured and five more are missing after an explosion at an [[industrial park]] housing several chemical companies in [[Leverkusen]], [[North Rhine-Westphalia|NRW]], [[Germany]]. [https://www.washingtonpost.com/world/explosion-at-chemical-complex-in-german-city-of-leverkusen/2021/07/27/3bf6e112-eeb7-11eb-81b2-9b7061a582d8_story.html (''The Washington Post'')]
*[[2021 California wildfires]]
**The [[Dixie Fire]] grows to 208,206 acres, which is larger than the size of [[New York City]]. [https://www.sfgate.com/california-wildfires/article/California-Dixie-Fire-wildfire-camera-video-16342905.php (''San Francisco Chronicle'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Bangladesh]]
****[[Bangladesh]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 258 deaths from [[COVID-19]], thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 19,779. [https://www.dhakatribune.com/bangladesh/2021/07/27/fatalities-hit-yet-another-high-in-bangladesh-as-258-die-of-covid-in-a-day (''Dhaka Tribune'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Indonesia]]
****[[Indonesia]] reports a record 47,128 recoveries and 2,069 deaths from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of recoveries to 2.596 million and the nationwide death toll to 86,835. [https://news.detik.com/berita/d-5658978/kematian-rekor-tembus-2-ribu-ini-data-lengkap-corona-27-juli?tag_from=wpm_nhl_10 (detikNews)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iran]]
****[[Iran]] reports a record for the second consecutive day of 34,951 new cases of COVID-19, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 3.758 million. [https://gulfnews.com/world/mena/iran-hits-record-for-new-covid-19-cases-for-second-day-running-1.81004173 (''Gulf News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Japan]]
****[[Tokyo]] reports a record 2,848 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours. [https://www.cbsnews.com/news/covid-tokyo-olympics-record-cases/ (CBS News)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kazakhstan]]
****[[Kazakhstan]] reports a record 6,797 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 542,703. [https://apa.az/en/xeber/asia-news/daily-covid-19-case-count-at-6797-in-kazakhstan-354645 (Azerbaijan Press Agency)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Kuwait]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Kuwait]] announces that it will ban unvaccinated people from travelling internationally beginning on August 1. However, the rule exempts children under the age of 16, those with a health ministry certificate saying that they cannot be vaccinated, and pregnant women who have a proof of pregnancy certificate. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/kuwait-bans-unvaccinated-citizens-traveling-abroad-2021-07-27/ (Reuters)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Saudi Arabia]]
****[[Saudi Arabia]] will require [[COVID-19 vaccine|COVID-19 vaccinations]] for people to access workplaces and attend social events. The order will come into effect on August 1. [https://english.aawsat.com/home/article/3100866/saudi-arabia-mandates-vaccination-certificate (''Asharq Al-Awsat'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Uzbekistan]]
****[[Uzbekistan]] reports a record 789 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 125,784. [https://m.akipress.com/news:660943:Uzbekistan_records_789_new_coronavirus_cases/ (AKIPress)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North America]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Cuba]]
****[[COVID-19 vaccination in Cuba]]
*****Over 8,900,000 people in [[Cuba]] have received a dose of the [[Abdala (vaccine)|Abdala]] and [[Soberana 02]] [[vaccine]]. [https://www.cadenagramonte.cu/english/show/articles/33180:more-than-8-900-000-covid-19-vaccine-doses-already-administered-in-cuba (Radio Cadena Agramonte)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Washington, D.C.]]
*****The [[White House]] issues an indoor [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] for staff amid the spread of the [[SARS-CoV-2 lineage B.1.617|Lineage B.1.617]] [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]]. [https://www.axios.com/white-house-reimposes-mask-mandate-2378a946-cb95-419c-af73-ea320ce99a7f.html (Axios)]
*****[[United States Secretary of Homeland Security|U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security]] [[Alejandro Mayorkas]] cancels in-person events and will self-isolate after coming in contact with an official in [[United States Department of Homeland Security|the department]] who later tested positive for COVID-19. [https://www.politico.com/news/2021/07/27/mayorkas-cancels-in-person-events-covid-500928 (Politico)] 
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Arkansas]]
*****The [[Arkansas Children's Hospital]] reports 24 hospitalizations due to COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, a new single-day record. [https://www.thv11.com/article/news/health/coronavirus/arkansas-childrens-record-high-covid-hospitalizations/91-665d4544-63b5-45f5-96aa-5b9f2ca84bb1 (KTHV-TV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Illinois]]
*****The [[Chicago Department of Public Health]] adds [[Alabama]], [[Alaska]], [[Arizona]], [[Kansas]], [[Mississippi]], [[Oklahoma]], [[Tennessee]], [[Texas]], and [[Wyoming]] to their travel advisory amid an increase in the number of COVID-19 cases. [https://www.newsweek.com/chicago-adds-nine-new-states-travel-advisory-list-delta-variant-cases-rise-1613697 (''Newsweek'')]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Mississippi]]
*****[[Mississippi Department of Corrections]] commissioner [[Burl Cain]] announces that [[Mississippi|the state]] will suspend visits to prisons as part of an effort to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://mississippitoday.org/2021/07/27/mississippi-department-of-corrections-cancels-prison-visitation-to-prevent-spread-of-covid/ (Mississippi Today)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Missouri]]
*****[[Kansas City, Missouri|Kansas City]] will reimpose their [[Face masks during the COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|mask mandate]] amidst a rise of COVID-19 cases in [[Missouri]]. [https://www.kansascity.com/news/coronavirus/article253075093.html (''Kansas City Star'')]
****[[Centers for Disease Control and Prevention|U.S. CDC]] director [[Rochelle Walensky]] announces that residents, including vaccinated Americans, are recommended to wear masks in indoor public spaces amid the spread of the Delta variant. [https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2021/07/27/1021206558/cdc-expected-to-change-mask-guidance-for-vaccinated-people-including-in-schools (NPR)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Iceland]], [[Travel restrictions related to the COVID-19 pandemic]]
****[[Iceland]] begins to require international travellers who have been [[COVID-19 vaccination in Iceland|vaccinated]] or who have recovered from COVID-19 to present a negative [[Polymerase chain reaction|PCR]] or [[Rapid antigen test|Antigen]] test result from the previous 72 hours due to the spread of the Delta variant. [https://www.schengenvisainfo.com/news/starting-from-july-27-iceland-brings-back-requirement-of-covid-19-test-results-for-vaccinated-travellers/ (Schengen Visa Info)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]], [[NHS COVID-19]]
****The [[United Kingdom]] eases its [[quarantine]] rules for essential workers in many fields who no longer need to quarantine for 10 days if they are fully [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United Kingdom|vaccinated]] and only need to receive a COVID-19 test after the previous rules led to a shortage of workers. [https://thehill.com/policy/international/565050-uk-easing-quarantine-rules-for-essential-workers (''The Hill'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Chile]]
***[[Chile]] reports 753 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, the lowest daily total in the country since April 2020. [http://www.china.org.cn/world/Off_the_Wire/2021-07/28/content_77655796.htm (China.org)]

'''International relations'''
*[[North Korea–South Korea relations]]
**[[North Korea|North]] and [[South Korea]] restore [[Seoul–Pyongyang hotline|hotlines]] between the two countries, more than a year after [[Pyongyang]] cut ties in June 2020. The move comes after months of correspondence by letters of negotiations between South Korean president [[Moon Jae-in]] and North Korean Supreme Leader [[Kim Jong-un]] in an attempt to improve relations between the two countries. [https://www.reuters.com/world/china/south-north-korea-have-restored-once-severed-hotline-blue-house-2021-07-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[2020 Hong Kong national security law|Hong Kong national security law]]
**A court in [[Hong Kong]] found 24-year-old Tong Ying-kit, the first person to be charged under the national security law, guilty of terrorism and secession after [[vehicle ramming attack|driving his motorcycle]] into police. [https://www.dw.com/en/hong-kong-first-guilty-verdict-under-national-security-law/a-58655014 (DW)] [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-07-27/hong-kong-court-set-to-deliver-verdict-in-first-security-trial (Bloomberg)]
*The trial against Cardinal [[Giovanni Angelo Becciu]] and ten others for financial crimes opens in the [[Holy See]]. Becciu and a monsignor are the only two to appear in court in person. Becciu denied any wrongdoing and the trial was adjourned. [[Pope Francis]] had previously stripped Becciu of his immunity and approved his indictment. Becciu's lawyers asked the court not to order the Cardinal's arrest. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/accused-cardinal-court-vatican-fraud-trial-opens-is-adjourned-2021-07-27/ (Reuters)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2020 Summer Olympics]]
**[[Bermuda at the 2020 Summer Olympics]], [[Triathlon at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Bermuda|Bermudian]] [[Olympic triathlon|triathlete]] [[Flora Duffy]] wins the [[Triathlon at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's|Women's event]], giving [[Bermuda at the Olympics|Bermuda its first Olympic gold metal]]. [https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/oympics-triathlon-duffy-wins-womens-gold-2021-07-26/ (Reuters)]
**[[Turkmenistan at the 2020 Summer Olympics]], [[Weightlifting at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***[[Turkmenistan|Turkmen]] [[weightlifter]] [[Polina Guryeva]] gets second place in the [[Weightlifting at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Women's 59 kg|Women's 59 kg event]], winning [[Turkmenistan at the Olympics|Turkmenistan its first Olympic medal]]. [https://apnews.com/article/2020-tokyo-olympics-sports-health-coronavirus-pandemic-turkmenistan-c197b8c867bca8ffa2902a830e60d573 (AP News)]
**[[North Macedonia at the 2020 Summer Olympics]], [[Taekwondo at the 2020 Summer Olympics]]
***[[North Macedonia|Macedonian]] [[Taekwondo|professional Taekwondo practitioner]] [[Dejan Georgievski]] wins second place in the [[Taekwondo at the 2020 Summer Olympics – Men's +80 kg|Men's +80 kg]], earning [[North Macedonia at the Olympics|North Macedonia its first Olympic silver medal]]. It is also the first medal the country has won after its [[Prespa agreement|renaming in 2018]] as well as the country's second medal overall. [https://apnews.com/article/2020-tokyo-olympics-gold-medals-0727-8ff24fb1ab8cc41324a874dd4d24ea76 (Associated Press)]
